one_liner: Abandoned (2020) Arrow-columnar C++ GIS engine with GeoPandas-style Python API; claims 7x single-thread and 24x multi-thread over 2020 GeoPandas.
what_it_does: Arctern is a spatial-temporal analytics framework from Zilliz: a C++ library (libarctern) exposing PostGIS-style vector functions (ST_Within, ST_Contains, ST_Intersects, ST_Intersection, ST_Buffer, ST_Area, ST_Distance, ST_HausdorffDistance, ST_MakeValid, ST_Transform and about 40 more) that take and return Apache Arrow arrays of WKB geometries. A Cython layer feeds a GeoSeries/GeoArray that mimics GeoPandas's interface, plus PySpark bindings, map rendering (heatmaps, choropleths via OSMesa or EGL) and an optional CUDA backend for a dozen predicates and measures. It is not a drop-in C++ library for geometry code: the API is batch-only over Arrow arrays, and from Python it is GeoPandas-like but not GeoPandas.
how_it_is_fast: On the CPU path the geometry work is still GDAL/OGR (createFromWkb, then OGRGeometry::Within/Contains/Intersects/IsValid, which call GEOS), so the speedup comes from running whole columns through C++ over Arrow WKB buffers instead of looping over Shapely objects in Python, plus a few shortcuts (for example a closed-form point-in-circle test for Within against a circular CurvePolygon). ST_IndexedWithin builds a GEOS STRtree or Quadtree for point-in-polygon joins. The optional GPU path implements Within, Intersects, Distance, Area and similar predicates as CUDA functors over decoded Arrow buffers. How the multi-thread mode is achieved is not documented; I found no thread pool or OpenMP in the C++ GIS code, the Cython layer or the GeoSeries Python I read.
when_to_use: Studying or reviving a columnar, Arrow-native design for batch spatial predicates over millions of WKB geometries; the C++ is Apache-2.0 and can be mined for ideas
Legacy 2020-era stacks pinned to pre-vectorised GeoPandas (before 0.8 added PyGEOS) where per-row Python loops over Shapely dominate run time
Experiments with CUDA spatial predicates (st_within.cu, st_intersects.cu, st_distance.cu) on Arrow data, if you can still build against CUDA 10-era toolchains
Point-in-polygon joins via ST_IndexedWithin (GEOS STRtree or Quadtree) in a pipeline that already speaks Arrow
when_not_to_use: Any new project: the repo has had no commits since 2020-06-23, the roadmap (distributed GeoSeries, KNN, trajectories) was never finished here, and open bug reports from 2020-2021 are unanswered

As a replacement for current GeoPandas: GeoPandas 1.0 (June 2024) runs on Shapely 2's vectorised C core, so the 2020 baseline that produced the 24x claim no longer exists and no newer comparison is published
When you want faster geometry algorithms rather than less Python overhead: the CPU predicates are GEOS via GDAL/OGR, so per-geometry cost is roughly GEOS's; TG or GeoRepair target that directly
Environments without conda: the build expects CONDA_PREFIX for GDAL, Arrow and GEOS headers, compiles with -Werror, and the render module needs OSMesa/GLU (CPU) or EGL/GL plus CUDA (GPU)
Windows or aarch64: CMake recognises only x86_64 and ppc64le; other targets fall through as 'unknown'

integration.form: shared lib (libarctern; static with STATIC_LIB_SWITCH) plus Cython Python package and PySpark module
integration.dependencies: GDAL/OGR (with GEOS), Apache Arrow, GEOS C++ index headers, miniz, stb; OSMesa and GLU for CPU rendering; CUDA 10+, GL and EGL for the GPU build; conda environment for headers and libs
integration.min_toolchain: C++14 (CMake sets CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 14; Cython extension built with -std=c++11), CMake 3.12+, CUDA 10 for GPU
integration.platforms: Linux x86_64 and ppc64le (ppc64le adds -mfloat128); macOS detected in CMake but not documented as supported; no Windows or aarch64 path
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — the Python GeoSeries copies GeoPandas's interface for the supported operations, but it is a separate package with its own WKB-in-Arrow storage, and GeoDataFrame, sjoin and many GeoPandas features are missing

gotchas: The CPU kernels round-trip every geometry WKB -> OGRGeometry -> (GEOS) per call, so chained operations pay parse and serialise costs each time; the speedup is from batching, not from a new algorithm
index_builder.cpp includes GEOS's C++ headers (geos/indexStrtree.h, geos::index::strtree::STRtree) rather than the GEOS C API, which ties it to the GEOS version of 2020 conda builds
Release builds add -O3 and -D_ARROW_ARRAY_SIZE=1073741824; Debug builds cap Arrow chunks at 16M, so behaviour around very large columns differs between build types
The README's headline 36x GPU figure is GPU vs Arctern's own CPU code, not vs GeoPandas or GEOS
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Rarely. TG beats GEOS on point-in-polygon throughput itself and is a small, maintained C library; GeoRepair and qdgeo target GEOS's slow validity and overlay operations directly. Arctern is only relevant if you want an Arrow-columnar, GeoPandas-shaped batch layer (or its CUDA predicates) and accept an abandoned GDAL/GEOS-based codebase.
verified_claims_summary: First-party README claim for v0.2.0: 24x average speedup over GeoPandas with multi-threading and 7x single-threaded across GeoSeries operations; the per-operation bar chart spans about 2.3x (geom_equals) to about 61x (is_simple) multi-threaded, and single-threaded geom_equals is slower than GeoPandas (about 0.6x). Dataset, hardware, thread count, compiler and GeoPandas version are not stated; given the June 2020 timing, the baseline was GeoPandas before 0.8 (June 24, 2020) added optional PyGEOS vectorisation, so it looped over Shapely 1.x objects in Python.
status_note: Abandoned since 2020-06-23 (v0.2.0, 103 stars, 8 open issues) but Apache-2.0; heavy conda/GDAL/Arrow build makes it a source of ideas rather than something to vendor.
